summary: Most players like the Six Zero Coral Pro 16mm for its control, easy resets and dinks, and grit that spins well and lasts. The main complaint is dead spots, especially near the top of the face, which many report and some reduce with added weight. Power is moderate, so it suits placement and kitchen players more than big hitters.

Players mostly love the 11SIX24 Ultré Power 2 for its spin, pop and power, plus a large sweet spot and grit that lasts. The downsides are a stiff, muted feel that bothers a good number of players and pop that can be hard to control on resets and drops. Often better with some weight added, and it suits players who like a lively paddle.

Players say spin from durable grit is the main draw for the 11SIX24 Vapor Power 2, along with power, a generous sweet spot and decent control, often once weight is added. Complaints include dead spots along the top edge, pop that is hard to control, and a stiff or numb feel for some. A few faces delaminated.

Players mostly praise the Vatic Pro Prism Flash as a soft, controlling paddle with a forgiving sweet spot and low swing weight, popular as a first or step-up paddle at a low price. Players often say it lacks power, so players must supply their own, and the grit wears off within months. Some also report cores breaking down.

Players mostly like the Six Zero Ruby for spin and control, with easy resets and dinks and a plush feel. Durability is the main complaint: many report the grit wearing smooth and pop fading after several months, and a few core crushed or delaminated. Some find it head heavy or short on power for hand battles.

Players mainly like the Six Zero Coral 16mm for control, with forgiving resets, drops and dinks and power that stays easy to manage. Complaints are durability, mostly edge guards separating, plus dead spots over time, and some find it short on power or the sweet spot small. It tends to suit players coming from poppier paddles.

Players like the Honolulu J2CR for spin, control and a large, forgiving sweet spot with a soft touch. The main complaint is the grit: it is applied inconsistently and some units went smooth within weeks or months, while others stayed gritty after heavy use. Honolulu usually replaced weak units, though not always easily.

Most players enjoy the Honolulu J6CR for its spin, pop and power with a big sweet spot. The main downside is the grit, which is inconsistent between units and faces and wore smooth within a few months for some, while others saw no change. A few report face damage or delamination and unhelpful support. Some find it head heavy until weighted.

Players widely praise the Vatic Pro V-Sol Pro as a budget paddle with good control, plus easy power and pop, often seen as a clear step up from the Prism Flash. Complaints are few: the grit fades with time, and a small number of players had delamination or a small sweet spot. It suits players wanting value.

Players mostly praise the 11SIX24 Vapor Power for easy power, a large sweet spot and good control, often without much adjustment. Downsides are a stiff feel that some found hard on the arm, and a few said it lacked spin or was hard to control. Most reports of durability are good, though a few cores crushed.

Players mainly like the Six Zero Double Black Diamond Control for control and fast hands, with good resets and dinks and enough power when needed. The 16mm is described as more forgiving than the 14mm. The main complaints are difficulty controlling pop-ups and long balls for some, and grit that wears for a few.

Players like the Bread & Butter Loco Hybrid for power, heavy spin, fast hands and a big sweet spot. The downsides are pop that makes dinks and resets hard to control for some, and grit that wears quickly, with a few calling it head heavy. It takes some sessions to dial in and suits attacking players.

Spin is what most players love about the 11SIX24 Hurache-X Power 2, with grit that lasts for many and good power and pop. The main complaints are delamination or disbonding, reported by several within weeks, and a dead zone near the top of the face. Replacements from 11SIX24 were usually quick.

Players praise the Joola Perseus Pro IV for power, pop and a forgiving sweet spot, and some find it controllable. Durability is the main complaint: many report core crush, loosening edge guards or a worn surface, sometimes needing repeated replacements. Some also find it too poppy for the soft game.

Players mostly love the Pickleball Apes Pulse for control on drops, resets and dinks, with a soft feel and a large sweet spot that improves after break-in. The main complaint is durability, with several reports of core crush or delamination, though the company replaced them quickly. Some found power lacking at first.

Players praise the Enhance MPP Turbo for control, a good sweet spot and strong value at about $100. The main complaint is delamination or disbonding, with several faces bubbling or separating, and the grit is not durable for some. Warranty replacements were usually honored, and a few mention long waits for delivery.

Players mostly like the Six Zero Black Opal 14mm for easy power and spin. The most common complaint is a small sweet spot that makes resets and volleys tougher and rewards centered hits, though some say it is overstated. It suits players who can hit centered and want power.

Most players enjoy the Luzz Cannon for its pop, power and spin, and often compare it favourably to a Joola Perseus Pro IV at a lower price. The downsides are that the power can be hard to control, particularly at the kitchen, and a small sweet spot for some. It feels stiff until broken in and suits hard hitters more than beginners.

Players like the Luzz Pro 4 Inferno for pop, power and a forgiving feel. Durability is the main complaint: several report rattling, hollow or dead faces and delamination, plus grit fading within months. Luzz often replaced faulty paddles, though some got no reply.

Players who like the 11SIX24 Pegasus Power describe a forgiving, light paddle with fast hands at the kitchen and power on demand. Some found it stiff or too poppy and hard to control, and a couple of cores crushed. It suits players who want a quick, forgiving power paddle.

Most players rave about its spin, and many also find it forgiving with good control and easy power. The main downsides are durability, with a few reports of a loosened edge guard, broken handle or worn surface, and a couple of players who found it hard to control. A few also dislike the handle.

Most players like its pop, strong spin and gritty surface, and several call it their favourite paddle. The common catch is that it can be too poppy or stiff, and a few found it light or underpowered out of the box. Grit wear is slight for most, and one reported elbow pain.

Players like its easy power, and many are surprised by how much control it has for a power paddle. Durability is the biggest worry: several report core crush, lost pop, cracks or edge guard problems within a few months. A few also notice dead spots off the sweet spot and an odd handle.

Most players like the mix of power and control, and many say it comes alive once weight is added to open up the sweet spot. Some found the stock paddle off or the sweet spot tight at first, and a few reported durability problems such as lost grit or going dead. It suits both singles and doubles for several players.

Most players love how fast it is in the hands, with good control and plenty of power, and many say it plays best with weight added since stock it feels light. The main downside is durability, mostly edge guards coming loose or a cracked edge, and one player saw the face wear smooth. Players often call it great value.

Most players praise its spin, control and large sweet spot, with a dense, muted feel and moderate power. Some find it so muted that it feels dead or less poppy than other paddles. Durability is the main complaint, with a few units rattling or loose parts needing warranty replacement, and one player said it softens in summer heat.

Most players like its spin, power and pop, and several find it a step up from the V-Sol Pro. The main complaint is grit durability, with many reporting the face going smooth after a few games to a few weeks. Some also find it too poppy or hard to control on drops.

Players' reviews are mixed. Fans like its power and pop with decent control, and some say it is arm-friendly, especially with added weight. The most repeated complaint is that it feels stiff or boardy, and a few found it hard to control, with a smaller sweet spot and a face that wears smooth.

Most players love its spin and drive power, and many call it their main paddle. Some find it head heavy or too poppy for resets and touch shots, and a few notice the grit wearing down after a few months. Several mention good value.

Most players love its soft, plush feel and control, especially for dinks, drops and resets, with enough power on full swings. The main downside is that it is on the heavy, head-heavy side, which a few found slow in hand battles, and adding weight makes it firmer. Some prefer other 11SIX24 paddles.

Most players like its power and pop, saying it works best with added weight and is great value. Durability is the main complaint, mostly edge guards coming loose, which Ronbus replaced under warranty, plus a couple reports of power dropping or wear. Some find the stock paddle unstable or too poppy for drops.

Players like its spin and consistent, dense feel, with an easy soft game. Many say it is head heavy and not as powerful as expected. Durability is the main complaint, with a few units going muted or rattling soon after purchase, and a couple found the handle stiff or the dead spots noticeable.

Most players are happy with its power, often described as a plush, Prism-like feel with more power, plus good control and spin that has lasted for some players. A couple found it weak or nothing special, and one found a smaller sweet spot and harder resets. It also gathers ball debris on the face for one player.

Most players love its feel, control and power, calling it plusher than the original Vapor Power, and several made it their main paddle. The clear downside is durability, with a few reporting core crush after a short time. A couple also had resets go into the net at first.

Most players like its control, spin and power, and some say the grit holds up well. Durability is the main concern, with a couple of players reporting it breaking after several months. A few found the sweet spot small or noticed dead spots around the edges.

Players are split. Fans like the hand speed, balance and tennis-friendly shape, and several are happy after months of use. The main complaint is durability: many report core crush, lost pop or dead areas within months, and a few felt it was pricey for how long it lasted.

Many players like its control, grit and dink-friendly feel, and some say the grit lasts well. The most repeated complaint is a lack of power, especially on smashes and returns, and a few found it stiff or unstable. Players coming from the original Ruby are divided.

Most players love its power and control, with good spin and a decent sweet spot, and a few call it their favourite paddle. Some had durability problems such as cracked end caps or edge-guard bubbles needing warranty replacement. A few found it hard to control on dinks or resets, or preferred a Boomstik.

Most players are happy with it, citing power, control and a good sweet spot, and several say it holds up well after months of play. A few had trouble: one cracked edge with a refused warranty claim, and one preferred a different paddle with a bigger sweet spot. One player said it eased elbow pain.

Players are strongly positive, praising its soft, dense feel, control, spin and quick hands, with easier dinks and resets and fewer pop-ups. The main caveat is modest power for some, with one saying put-away power stayed low even with weight and another saying serves need more.

Most players like it, citing power, soft touch at the kitchen and a poppy but controllable feel, and one had no elbow pain. Some find it stiff, hollow or loud, and a few mention an older unit going duller or losing spin. Weight at 3 and 9 helped one player.

Players like its huge pop and light, low swing weight, and some also praise its control. The main complaints are a small, unforgiving sweet spot and poor durability, with several reporting it losing pop, rattling, or delaminating within months. A few also found the long handle awkward.

Players are very positive, praising its control, spin and a large sweet spot with a dense feel and good pop. Several own the widebody and call it their best or main paddle. A couple said it was narrow at first until weight was added, and one was lukewarm but liked the value.

Most players love it, with the 14.3 described as more forgiving and controllable and the 12.7 as fast with power when needed. A few found a small sweet spot on the 12.7 or dead spots on one 14.3. Some mentioned good durability and a high price.

Most players like its spin, pop and softer feel, with easy drops and dinks and good control. Some found it hard to control at first, a little light or twisty off-centre, and a few were lukewarm on its power compared with the Ultré. Weighting it helped several, and one found it not worth the price.
Players mostly love the Black Ace Pro, and a couple say it let them keep playing through tennis elbow. A few report dimples in the face from normal use.
Players mostly like the Roadrunner for fast hands, spin and a controlled feel, though several find it short on pop and a few note a smaller sweet spot. A couple saw the grit or spin fade over time.

Players find the Perseus Pro V good for control and touch, but several report durability problems such as a crushed core or crackling edge, and a few coming from the Pro IV saw little gain or preferred it.
Players describe the Bantam TKO-C as powerful and poppy, but most find the sweet spot small and the soft game at the kitchen hard to keep consistent.
Players find the Boomstik Elongated very powerful, but some find it too poppy for reliable resets and soft play, and a few say it feels head-heavy or that the grit wore.
Players mostly like the TruFoam Genesis for quick, manoeuvrable hands and a good soft game at the kitchen.
Players describe the Fuse Hybrid-W as soft and hollow feeling once broken in, with easy dinks and resets, though opinions on its power are split.
Players who like the Quanta R2 point to pop and quick hands, but several report durability trouble, mainly edge guards coming loose or foam falling out, leading to warranty claims.
Players find the Q2 Elongated poppy and powerful stock, and several added weight for stability or extra punch.
Players mostly like the Pegasus Jelly Bean for control, a forgiving sweet spot and good dinking, though a couple find it a bit soft or weak on hard drives.
Players are all positive on the Alpha Pro, finding it powerful yet consistent on drops and resets, and a couple have made it their main paddle.
Players mostly find the 16mm Elongated easier for dinks, drops and resets than the Pro Power Elongated, with somewhat less pop, though a couple find it heavy and slow to get comfortable.
Players mostly like the Scorpeus 3S for pop and soft-game control, though a couple report it losing responsiveness or crunching after heavy play.
Players mostly like the Scorpeus Pro IV, with several naming it a favorite or main paddle. A couple report problems, one with shoulder tendinitis and one with a chipped frame.
Players describe the Harmony as a soft-feeling, manoeuvrable all-court paddle that is low on power.
Players find the Boomstik Widebody very powerful and poppy, and several call it the best fit for their game, though a couple find dinks and soft shots harder to dial in.
Players are very positive on the Spitfire Widebody, praising quick hands at the kitchen, spin and a forgiving face, though a couple note a hollow sound.
Players say the Vapor Jelly Bean 2 has dead or unstable top corners and a sweet spot that is hard to find unless weight is added, though a couple still love it.
Players describe the Hush as very powerful with lots of spin but hard to control, sending balls long unless fundamentals are solid.
Players, several moving up from cheap paddles, get more spin and a forgiving feel from the SweetSpot Pro, though it is not a power paddle.
Players describe the Pro Ultimate Hyper as a soft, quick-in-hand paddle with somewhat less power than other Gearbox models.
Players mostly like the Quanta R1, but several describe adding weight, with one finding it unforgiving without it.
Players report the P1 Hybrid's edge guard coming loose or separating, one out of the box and another after the first use.
